suppose on all solutions of some system of first-order P$\Delta$Es,

This implies the
multisymplecticity of the system.
For a general variational problem, its multisymplectic  form may be defined on the total prolongation space.

issues.failure_explanation: The passage asserts that an arbitrary vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form conserved on solutions can 'be written' in the displayed shape, in which each summand pairs only the specific vertical one-forms $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm v}(\mathrm{S}_i^{-1}u^\alpha)$ and $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}} u^\beta$. Within the paper's own definitions, a vertically closed $(p-1,2)$-form on the prolongation space is an arbitrary finite combination $c^{\alpha\beta}_{\mathbf{J}\mathbf{K}}(\mathbf{n},[\mathbf{u}])\,\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^\alpha_{\mathbf{J}}\wedge\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^\beta_{\mathbf{K}}\wedge(\partial_{n^i}\intp\mathrm{vol})$; e.g. $\omega=\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^1_{(2,0)}\wedge\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^1_{(0,0)}\wedge h_1$ (constant coefficient) is vertically closed but has no representation of the form (eq:multiform). The paper itself concedes that for a general variational problem the multisymplectic form 'may be defined on the total prolongation space'. Hence the asserted normal form is a genuine restriction, and the extraction of the standard forms $\kappa^i$ and the concluded multisymplecticity of the system only follow for forms already of that shape. (The ambient space is also stated as $\mathbb{Z}^p\times U$, on which the shifted one-forms $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}(\mathrm{S}_i^{-1}u^\alpha)$ are not even defined.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the statement to forms of the standard type (as the paper's own later terminology 'standard multisymplectic forms' does) and derive multisymplecticity only for that class, or prove a genuine normal-form theorem; no other result in the paper depends on the unrestricted version.
issues.overall_effect: The converse half of Section 5 (vertically closed conserved form ⟹ standard multisymplectic forms $\kappa^i$ ⟹ multisymplecticity, and the route to first-order fully degenerate Lagrangians of the form \eqref{lp} for linear systems) is established only for forms already of the standard type; for general vertically closed conserved forms the claimed deduction does not follow from the source.
issues.title: Arbitrary vertically closed (p−1,2)-forms claimed to take the 'standard' coordinate form
issues.why_classification: A local rewording that restricts the claim to standard-type forms (which the paper already isolates in \eqref{kap}) preserves every subsequent result and guarantee; no new lemma or reconstruction is needed.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
First of all, notice that $\ker
(\mcI^{\vartriangle})=\operatorname{im}
(\dDh)$, which is an
immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:ii}.

issues.failure_explanation: The claimed homotopy identity $h^{k+1,l}_{\uph}(\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}\sigma)+\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}(h^{k,l}_{\uph}\sigma)=\sigma$ is asserted for all $1\le k\le p$, but at $k=p$ it is false: $\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}\sigma=0$ identically on $\Omega^{p,l}$ (there are no $(p+1)$-forms in the exterior algebra on $p$ symbols), so the identity would force $\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}(h^{p,l}_{\uph}\sigma)=\sigma$ for every $(p,l)$-form, i.e. every $(p,l)$-form would be horizontally exact. This contradicts the structure of the augmented complex: by \eqref{coch}, $\mathcal{I}^{\vartriangle}\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}=0$, while $\mathcal{I}^{\vartriangle}(\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^\alpha\wedge\mathrm{vol})=\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}u^\alpha\wedge\mathrm{vol}\neq0$, so such forms are not in $\operatorname{im}(\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}})$. The identity can therefore only hold for $k\le p-1$. Moreover, the proof opens by deriving $\ker(\mathcal{I}^{\vartriangle})=\operatorname{im}(\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}})$ 'as an immediate consequence of \eqref{eq:ii}', but \eqref{eq:ii} is the decomposition for the differential bicomplex of Section 2, not for the difference complex under construction; the difference-case top-degree fact is exactly what the theorem must establish, so the exactness at the top degree $\Omega^{p,l}\to\mathscr{F}^l$ is never established by the given argument (the identity \eqref{eq:hohomo} itself is asserted, not derived).

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the homotopy identity \eqref{eq:hohomo} to $1\le k\le p-1$ and, for the top degree $k=p$, prove the decomposition $\sigma=\mathcal{I}^{\vartriangle}\sigma-\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}\tau$ from the kernel characterization of the difference interior Euler operator (as in Hydon–Mansfield 2004 and the thesis \cite{Pe2013}, both cited by the paper), then use it in place of the miscited \eqref{eq:ii} here and in the proof of Theorem thm:added-4.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed exactness of the augmented horizontal complex $0\to\Omega^{0,l}\to\cdots\to\Omega^{p,l}\xrightarrow{\mathcal{I}^\vartriangle}\mathscr{F}^l\to0$ is not established by the source: the homotopy identity used is false at $k=p$, and the top-degree step $\ker(\mathcal{I}^\vartriangle)=\operatorname{im}(\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}})$ is supported only by a citation to the differential-case identity \eqref{eq:ii}. The proof of Theorem thm:added-4 likewise invokes this difference-case decomposition ('From \eqref{eq:ii}, we have $\mathrm{d}_{\mathrm{v}}\sigma=\delta^{\vartriangle}_{\upv}\sigma+\mathrm{d}^{\vartriangle}_{\mathrm{h}}\tau_1$'), so its argument inherits the same gap; the exactness on which the paper's coordinate-free Noether theorem and Hamiltonian existence arguments rely is thus left without a valid in-source proof.
issues.title: Proof of horizontal exactness (Theorem thm:added-3) fails at top degree
issues.why_classification: The theorem's conclusion (row exactness) is true and available in the literature the paper cites (Kupershmidt 1985; Hydon–Mansfield 2004; Peng's thesis, which the appendix explicitly follows), so a contained, nontrivial repair—restricting the homotopy identity to $k\le p-1$ and supplying the standard top-degree Euler-operator argument—restores the theorem with no loss of the advertised exactness; no advertised application must be abandoned, but a substantive missing argument must be supplied, which is more than a local routine fix.
